entries.answer:
[ERROR LIST]

- Line 117: `initWithConfig` creates `tokenizer` with `errdefer tokenizer.deinit()`, then transfers a value-copy of it into `components`; if `initWithComponents` fails after installing its own `errdefer tokenizer.deinit()`, both error defers deinitialize the same tokenizer-owned allocations, causing double-free/use-after-free behavior.[1]

- Line 121: `SignalPropagationEngine.init(allocator, undefined, undefined)` constructs a component using deliberately uninitialized dependencies; `initWithComponents` subsequently calls `provisional.deinit()` on that component. This invokes destruction on an object initialized with invalid dependency values.[1]

- Line 174: `signal_engine_rebound` is placed into `trainer.signal_engine`, then immediately overwritten by a second `SignalPropagationEngine.init(...)` result without calling `deinit()` on the first instance; resources owned by `signal_engine_rebound` are leaked.[1]

- Line 295: `loadDataset` counts every physical input line as a sample during its fallback scan, including malformed JSON, JSON without `"text"`, empty text, and non-tokenizable text.[1]

- Line 330: `appendDatasetRange` increments `line_index` for every physical line but appends only lines for which `extractDatasetText` returns text; therefore `start_valid_index` and `end_valid_index` are not valid-sample indexes despite their names. Dataset partitions are incorrect whenever any ignored line exists.[1]

- Line 346: A dataset containing one or more malformed/non-text lines can make `samples.items.len != samples_per_rank`, causing `loadDataset` to return `error.InvalidDatasetPartition` even when sufficient usable samples exist later in the file.[1]

- Line 276: `isUsableDatasetLine` performs the required tokenizability test but is never called by either dataset counting or dataset range extraction; the declared filtering rule is not applied.[1]

- Line 594: In distributed training, ranks with an empty final batch still execute `trainingStep` with `effective_batch_size = 1` and an all-zero input/target tensor whenever at least one other rank has data. Their zero-sample optimizer update is included in synchronization.[1]

- Line 691: Distributed weight aggregation averages per-rank deltas equally, rather than weighting them by each rank’s actual batch/sample count. Unequal shard sizes or final batches therefore produce a different update from training on the combined data.[1]

- Line 691: Only `weights_s` and `weights_t` are restored after cross-rank delta averaging; `velocity_s` and `velocity_t` remain rank-local after each optimizer step. Subsequent momentum-based updates diverge across ranks.[1]

- Line 514: `gpuAllReduceLayers`, the only function that synchronizes both model weights and velocity tensors, is never called.[1]

- Line 701: Embedding gradients and embedding parameter updates are applied locally in `propagateEmbeddingGradients` without any distributed reduction or synchronization; multi-rank training necessarily leaves embedding parameters divergent.[1]

- Line 1171: Futhark backward-operation return codes are discarded for `futhark_entry_batch_oftb_backward`; a failed backward call is treated as if it had produced a valid gradient pointer.[1]

- Line 1185: The return code of `futhark_entry_batch_gradients_full` is discarded; failures can silently skip the current layer’s gradients or leave `tup` null without propagating an error.[1]

- Lines 1201-1203: Return codes from all three tuple-projection calls are discarded. The code may continue with null gradient pointers after failed Futhark projections.[1]

- Line 1234: `emb.applyGradients(self.learning_rate, self.momentum)` is executed once per sample after gradients have been accumulated through prior samples in the same batch. Earlier accumulated gradients are therefore reapplied on every later iteration unless `applyGradients` independently clears them; no clearing occurs in this function after each update.[1]

- Line 921: `saved_vocab_size` is read from the checkpoint and then explicitly discarded; a checkpoint whose saved vocabulary is incompatible with the current tokenizer/model is accepted without validation.[1]

- Line 922: `saved_local_batch_size` is read from the checkpoint and then explicitly discarded; a checkpoint may be loaded under a different batch-size configuration without any compatibility check.[1]

- Line 987: `@enumFromInt(quality_byte)` converts unvalidated checkpoint data directly to `nsir.EdgeQuality`. An out-of-range byte produces an invalid enum value and can trigger a runtime safety failure.[1]

[END OF LIST]
